title: Constant-factor approximation for uniform Sparsest Cut
area: Approximation algorithms and hardness of approximation
formal: Do a universal \(C\ge 1\) and a randomized polynomial-time algorithm exist which, on every finite simple undirected graph G on \(n\ge 2\) vertices, output a nonempty proper set S with \(\varphi _{G}(S)\le C \min _{\varnothing \ne T\subsetneq V} \varphi _{G}(T)\), with probability at least \(2/3\)?
definitions: Here \(\varphi _{G}(S)=|E(S,V\setminus S)|/(|S|\cdot |V\setminus S|)\), where \(E(S,V\setminus S)\) is the set of edges having exactly one endpoint in S. The graph is supplied explicitly by an adjacency matrix. Polynomial time is measured in bit operations on every random tape; the same algorithm and constant must work for all graphs. The zero-optimum disconnected case requires returning a zero cut. Uniform refers to equal demand for each pair of vertices, not regularity of the graph.

context_blocks.text: Uniform Sparsest Cut balances a cut’s edge boundary against the number of separated pairs. It is a basic measure of the decomposability of a graph and a major test case for approximation algorithms.

The ARV result gives an \(O(\sqrt{\log  n})\) approximation, with a bound growing with the graph size. A constant factor would cross the remaining qualitative approximation barrier. Nonuniform pair demands, conductance normalized by volumes, and Small-Set Expansion have different targets and are not silently substituted here.

why: Determine whether a central graph-decomposition objective admits approximation independent of instance size.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
